title: WPMS/2869/2017 of Lakhpat Singh Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 2869 of 2017
Lakhpat Singh Ö Petitioner
Vs
State of Uttarakhand & others Ö Respondents
Mr. Dharmendra Barthwal, Advocate, present for the petitioner.
Mr. N.S. Pundir, Deputy Advocate, General, present for the State of Uttarakhand.
Honíble Manoj K. Tiwari, J. (Oral)
1. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused
the records.
2. According to the petitioner, he was granted
permission to pick River Bed Material (in short ìRBMî) from
River Alaknanda in District Pauri Garhwal in terms of
Uttarakhand River Training Policy. This permission was
granted to the petitioner on 19.11.2016, wherein it was
provided that this permission is being granted only for a period
of six months. According to the petitioner, permission was
granted for removing 19140 ton of RBM, as against which, he
could remove only 5482 ton of RBM upto 18.05.2017.
3. It is the contention of learned counsel for the
petitioner that due to unforeseen reasons, including judgment
rendered by this Court in a public interest litigation, he could
not undertake mining operations for more than two months
and moreover, there was a dispute raised by villagers regarding
approach road to the site. All these factors taken together
created a situation that petitioner could remove less than 33%
of the quantity of RBM, which was permitted to be removed.
4. It is the contention of the petitioner that he has
deposited royalty for the entire quantity of RBM for which
permission was granted, therefore, he submits that the time
limit indicated in the permission be extended by another six
months, so that he may be able to remove the remaining
amount of RBM.

2
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner confines his
prayer and submits that petitioner has made a representation
to District Magistrate, Pauri Garhwal on 05.11.2017 on which
no decision has been taken so far. He further submits that
District Magistrate be directed to look into the matter and take
appropriate decision.
6. On 17.11.2017, Mr. N.S. Pundir, learned Deputy
Advocate General was asked to seek instructions in the matter.
On instructions, he submits that representation made by the
petitioner is not traceable in the office of District Magistrate,
Pithoragarh.
7. Accordingly, the writ petition is disposed of with
liberty to petitioner to make a fresh representation to the
District Magistrate, Pauri Garhwal within two weeks from
today. If such a representation is made, District Magistrate
shall take appropriate decision thereupon, in accordance with
law, within three weeks thereafter.
